title: Two Isotopes, One Sample
summary: A sample holds two isotopes with different half-lives. Compare their numbers of nuclei and their activities as time passes.
statement:
A freshly made sample holds equal numbers of nuclei of two radioactive isotopes. Isotope X has a half-life of $$2.0\ \mathrm h$$ and isotope Y has a half-life of $$6.0\ \mathrm h$$. Neither decays into the other, and all the decay products are stable. The activity of an isotope is the number of its nuclei that decay per second.

## (a)

Find the ratio $$N_X/N_Y$$ of the numbers of nuclei left, $$6.0\ \mathrm h$$ after the sample was made.

## (b)

Find the ratio $$A_X/A_Y$$ of the two activities at that same time.

## (c)

How long after the sample was made are the two activities equal? Give the time in hours.
solution:
## (a)

After each half-life, half of the nuclei that were there are left. In $$6.0\ \mathrm h$$ isotope X goes through three half-lives and isotope Y through one. With $$N_0$$ nuclei of each at the start,

$$N_X=\frac{N_0}{8},\qquad N_Y=\frac{N_0}{2}.$$

$$\boxed{\frac{N_X}{N_Y}=\frac14=0.25.}$$

## (b)

The activity is not the number of nuclei. Each nucleus of an isotope has the same chance of decaying per second, the decay constant $$\lambda=\ln2/T$$, where $$T$$ is the half-life. So

$$A=\lambda N=\frac{\ln2}{T}\,N.$$

A nucleus of X is three times as likely to decay in the next second as a nucleus of Y, because its half-life is three times shorter:

$$\frac{A_X}{A_Y}=\frac{T_Y}{T_X}\,\frac{N_X}{N_Y}=3\times\frac14.$$

$$\boxed{\frac{A_X}{A_Y}=0.75.}$$

## (c)

At a time $$t$$ in hours,

$$\frac{A_X}{A_Y}=3\,\frac{2^{-t/2}}{2^{-t/6}}=3\times2^{-t/3}.$$

The ratio starts at 3 and falls. It equals 1 when $$2^{t/3}=3$$:

$$t=3\log_2 3\ \mathrm h=3\,\frac{\ln 3}{\ln 2}\ \mathrm h.$$

$$\boxed{t=4.75\ \mathrm h.}$$

Check with part (b): at $$6.0\ \mathrm h$$ the ratio has already fallen to $$0.75$$, so the activities were equal a little earlier than that.

a: After each half-life, half of the nuclei that were there are left.
Count the half-lives in $$6.0\ \mathrm h$$. Isotope X has had three and isotope Y has had one.
The fractions left are $$1/8$$ and $$1/2$$. The starting numbers are equal, so divide one fraction by the other.
b: Activity is decays per second. It depends on how many nuclei there are and on how likely each one is to decay.
Use $$A=\lambda N$$ with $$\lambda=\ln2/T$$, where $$T$$ is the half-life. The shorter half-life has the larger decay constant.
The ratio is $$(T_Y/T_X)(N_X/N_Y)$$. The first factor is 3 and the second is your answer to part (a).
c: Write the activity ratio at a general time $$t$$ in hours, using $$N=N_02^{-t/T}$$ for each isotope.
The ratio is $$3\times2^{-t/2}/2^{-t/6}=3\times2^{-t/3}$$. It starts at 3 and falls.
Set the ratio equal to 1, so $$2^{t/3}=3$$. Take logarithms to get $$t=3\ln3/\ln2$$.
